report.source_text: This patient was admitted to hospital and acyclovir 1.8 g daily by intravenous infusion was provided followed by oral valacyclovir 3 g per day. She received an intravitreal forscarnet injection (1.2 mg/0.05 mL). Close liaison was undertaken with clinical microbiology and genitourinary medicine. The HIV-positive result was discussed with the patient and antiretroviral therapy (ART) commenced.

Multiple areas of white retinal swelling in the posterior pole with macula involvement were apparent (figure 1) in the right eye. Obliterated arterioles with perivascular sheathing (Kyrieleis’ plaques)1 were detected (figures 1 and 2). Ultrasound showed bilateral RDs.

The patient was registered blind and has had input from social services and community occupational therapy including modifications to her home because of acquired visual loss.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A retired woman with 18-month history of left-sided herpes zoster ophthalmicus (HZO) and 7-month history of left keratouveitis presented with 4-week progressive right vision loss following a mechanical fall. Initial examination revealed no perception of light (NPL) in both eyes, right eye vitreous haze with multiple areas of white retinal swelling in the posterior pole involving the macula, obliterated arterioles with perivascular sheathing (Kyrieleis plaques), and left eye diffuse stromal corneal scarring with pigmented keratic precipitates and 360° posterior synechiae. Ultrasound confirmed bilateral retinal detachments. Workup revealed unrecognised advanced HIV infection (CD4 37 cells/µL, viral load 116,912 copies/mL). Aqueous humor PCR was positive for VZV DNA and negative for CMV and HSV, confirming VZV as the causative agent of the necrotising retinopathy. Treatment included intravenous acyclovir 1.8 g daily, oral valacyclovir 3 g/day, intravitreal foscarnet injection, and commencement of antiretroviral therapy. Despite treatment, after 1 week serum VZV DNA became negative but vision remained NPL bilaterally with inoperable retinal detachments, resulting in registration as blind with social services input.
